summary: T4's typed browser import API (importIcs, IcsImportSummary, IcsImportApiError, error-code type) was already present in committed code and satisfies every acceptance criterion; verified it with the packet test command and typecheck, and recorded completion in the plan status file.
follow_up: T5 can consume importIcs(api, calendarId, file) which throws IcsImportApiError with status and code (invalid_calendar_file | calendar_import_limit_exceeded | unknown); isCalendarAccessChange already covers 401/403/404/409 for the access-denial refresh behavior.
important_context: T4 implementation and tests pre-existed in commit f8c39b9 (Codex/ics import #2); this run verified them and recorded completion rather than writing new code.
importIcs sends the unmodified File as body with content-type text/calendar; charset=utf-8 to POST /api/v1/calendars/:calendar_id/import-ics, matching the approved architecture contract.
Unknown or malformed error envelopes map to IcsImportApiError with code 'unknown' and a client-owned message; server-provided text never surfaces to callers.
